title: PulseCheck — Slow Answers
objective: The newsletter sign-up always gives the same answer and never shows an error. Yet the database holds a PIN for the admin console. Recover it and unlock the console.

verifier.condition: The correct admin PIN — which exists only in the database and differs for every instance — is submitted to the admin unlock form.

weakness: A concatenated query in a response-identical endpoint can still be made to run a data-dependent delay, turning response time into a one-bit-at-a-time channel for exfiltration.
seededData: SQLite: subscribers table and a settings table with a per-instance 6-digit admin PIN. Unlock attempts are limited to 10 wrong guesses per instance.
hints: Compare how long different requests take. What could make a query slower only when something about the data is true?
You cannot read the PIN directly, but you can ask the database yes/no questions about it. Think about one character at a time.
The unlock form allows only a few wrong guesses, so guessing blindly is not an option — you have to extract it.
burpNotes: Measure response times in Repeater. This lab's database exposes sleep_ms(milliseconds) — SQLite has no built-in sleep, but many engines do — capped at 2 seconds per call. Scripting the extraction (Burp Intruder, Python requests, curl in a loop) is expected.
